posts.title: Work-Life Balance Isn't Real
posts.excerpt: Ever heard of a 'false dichotomy'? Work-life balance is one of the biggest ones out there. Here's what's really going on.
posts.content:
Hi,

Ever heard of a 'false dichotomy'?

A false dichotomy is a logical fallacy where someone pretends like there are only two options when that's not actually the case.

You'll recognise these:

- *"You're either with us or against us."*
- *"If you're not a vegan you hate animals."*
- *"I'd rather be healthy than rich."*

You can see that these are all objectively wrong — pretending you have to choose between two alternatives.

I'll add one more to the list:

**"Work-life balance"**

What are we even saying here?

Are you not alive while you're at work? Does your life stop when your work ends? Does your life end when your work starts?

We're both business owners. Some of the best ideas come while walking in nature, enjoying life, spending time with family, watching a movie.

Work is a part of life. **ESPECIALLY for business owners like you and I.** It never really stops. One bleeds into the other.

And that's not a problem — that's a feature.

Don't let anyone talk you into thinking this is weird or wrong.

Talk soon,

**The AKW Marketing Team**

posts.title: Stop Randomly Throwing Things
posts.excerpt: Adding more stuff is usually the worst thing you can do. Before you start adding — let's first figure out what's actually wrong.
posts.content:
Hi,

Whenever we do client work, there's always pressure to add things.

New pages.

New emails.

New content to their Google Business Profile.

New ad campaigns, angles, offers, guarantees, creatives and soooooo much more.

Just one problem.

**Adding more stuff is usually the worst thing you can do.**

Let's say you're a doctor. Patient comes in. His belly hurts.

You respond by throwing some opioids at him. After all, this makes total sense! Man is in pain. Opioids are good against pain. 1+1 = 2.

This is a great way to lose your medical license in a hurry.

You're supposed to figure out what is ACTUALLY wrong with the man — and then you come up with a treatment.

Blindly adding something to the mix will probably not help, and might even make things worse.

Same thing goes for marketing.

Before you start adding content to your Google Business Profile... let's first get a feeling for WHY you're not ranking #1 yet.

Before you start adding new campaigns to Google Ads... let's see how the current campaigns perform and what we could improve.

Before you start filling Meta with new creatives... let's see how the campaigns do right now and what elements we could double down on.

Stop randomly throwing pills at things. It ruins your results.

Diagnose first. Then treat.

Talk soon,

**The AKW Marketing Team**

posts.title: Google Wizards
posts.excerpt: People that help you rank in Google are really invested in upholding this image of themselves as arcane wizards. It's mostly BS. Here's the truth.
posts.content:
Hi,

Once upon a time, someone ranked their own website number 1 on Google for: *"Best looking man in Maastricht."*

As a joke they'd ask people to Google the term and they would always be amazed at this level of marketing sorcery.

One day they showed it to someone who asked: *"Wow, how do you do that!?"*

So they explained that it was pretty straightforward.

This was a mistake.

Because a guy overheard and started having a full-blown meltdown. Turns out he worked at some firm that did SEO for big companies, so this was apparently a touchy subject.

*"No, that's wrong, that's not the way it works at all! You clearly don't know what you're talking about!"*

Foaming at the mouth level angry.

The logical response? Just show him the ranking for that particular keyword.

Unsurprisingly — this did not go over well.

He started rattling off keywords his clients ranked for and the amount of 'backlinks' it took and his 'pagerank'.

Blablabla.

People that help you rank in Google are just really, really invested into upholding this image of themselves as arcane wizards hunched over a magic orb that no one has access to.

It's mostly BS.

SEO (Search Engine Optimization) is mostly just logical thinking. It really is.

**Logical thinking + elbow grease + time = better ranking.**

Don't let anyone fool you into thinking it's undoable for mere mortals. They're just BSing you 99% of the time.

Talk soon,

**The AKW Marketing Team**

posts.title: The Worst Number

This went on for **7 months**. Absolutely wrecked — because there was only 1 source of leads.

If you depend on referrals or word of mouth or Meta ads or Google Ads ALONE?

You're a disaster waiting to happen.

Don't do it to yourself. The stress isn't worth it.

Develop multiple lead sources. Because ONE is the worst number in business by far.

posts.title: No One Cares. Really.
posts.excerpt: We reviewed a business owner's sales presentation recently. It was beautiful, well organized, intricate. And it kind of sucked. Here's why.
posts.content:
Hi,

We were going over a client's sales presentation recently. Seeing if there was room for improvement.

The man had poured his heart into it. Went all out. Deserved an epic soundtrack.

So we got to the end and he asked the big question: *"So, what do you think?"*

And we had to tell him, in the most diplomatic way possible: *"Yeah... it kinda sucks. But we'll make it waaay better!"*

Don't get us wrong.

The presentation was beautiful. Well organized. Intricate. Covered alllllll the bases.

But here's the major problem that EVERY business owner faces:

**No one cares about our stuff nearly as much as WE care about our stuff.**

WE care about how the sausage is made. WE care how much work we put in. WE care about the effort. All the steps we DON'T skip.

But our clients? They genuinely don't care. They only care about **IF it works**. Not HOW it works.

Sales presentations should ALWAYS and ONLY be focused on proving that your thing works.

Forget the details. No one cares about details. Clients only care about results.

Best to double-check your sales presentation and keep this in mind.

Talk soon,

**The AKW Marketing Team**

posts.title: BMR

And it's easy to set up as well. Just align your keywords with your ad copy and voilà — you show up at the right time for the right word.

The ONLY thing you have to do to win as a local business is this:

**Be**

**More**

**Relevant**

That's it. Nothing else.

Set your marketing up so you're the most relevant person to call at the most relevant time.

posts.title: Easy Wins
posts.excerpt: If you run a local business, you're competing in an arena where the odds are tilted heavily in your favour. Here's why — and how to take full advantage.
posts.content:
Hi,

Andre Agassi's autobiography — *Open* — is a great book.

He describes his mental state when he was at the top of his game. The man would show up to a match, look at his opponent, and say in his mind: *"Why did this guy even show up? You know there's zero chance of winning. You're about to get rekt."*

And then he whooped them.

We get that same feeling whenever a local business owner asks us for help.

Because we know how to win in that arena. Every single time.

Think about this.

If you run a business on a **national level** you're usually competing against companies with entire marketing divisions. These people get up every day thinking about how to outmarket the competition.

If you run a business on a **local level** you're mostly competing against guys doing their job. Everyone knows that marketing is important and SHOULD be a priority... but there's 101 things that are also a priority. So marketing often goes on the backburner.

That's why it's such a slam-dunk opportunity to work with local businesses. Once you bring in someone that's exclusively focused on marketing, it's suddenly really easy to beat the competition. And the edge just gets bigger and bigger with every week that goes by.

Choose your battles and pick the ones you can win. It builds momentum, builds confidence, builds revenue.

Clients want to work with winners.

posts.title: If You Had To
posts.excerpt: If you HAD to sell something, if your life was on the line — how would you do it? Nothing sells as well as one specific thing.
posts.content:
Hi,

If you HAD to sell something, if your life was on the line...

...how would you do it?

Discounts? Hell no, seems desperate.

Adding value? Sounds great, but *howwww*?

Guarantees? Much better, but not the ultimate way.

Nothing — and we mean nothing — sells as well as a **demonstration**.

Doesn't matter where you live, doesn't matter who your target customer is. We humans are hardwired to believe what we see. If we see it? It's real. If we can't see it? It's conceptual. Not real. Fuggazi. Fairy dust.

So.

Whatever you do — you MUST find a way to demonstrate it.

Demo the product. The process. Your expertise.

Something.

Make it real.

You prove expertise by posting content. Videos are best. Short clips showing your work, your process, your results. Put them everywhere.

posts.title: First Thing
posts.excerpt: What's the first thing you do in the morning? And more importantly — what's the first thing your customers do?

posts.title: Smart Small, Big Dumb
posts.excerpt: Most marketing advice really really sucks. Here's what big companies actually did when they were small — and what you should do instead of copying Coca-Cola.
posts.content:
Hi,

Most marketing advice really really sucks.

We studied marketing for years. Then we started businesses. Tried to implement what we learned in school.

It was an unmitigated disaster.

Didn't get clients. Hardly got anyone to even look at the ads.

The ad salesman said: *"Yeah, you should run it very often. Veeeeeerrrrrrryyyyy often."*

Made sense. The guy got paid every time the ad ran.

Took a while to figure out that in school they teach you the strategy that companies like Coca-Cola use **right now**.

Just blast your ad and hope for the best.

Only issue is that Coca-Cola has a $600 million ad budget. And yours is probably a little less than that.

If you water a strategy down by a factor of one million, it doesn't tend to do as well.

Also, Coca-Cola has 10,000 people in their marketing department. You have one. Which is you. And you also have to do everything else!

So the real question is: *'how do big companies get so big?'* You don't go from zero to a $600 million budget without doing something right... right?

After a whole lot of research, they all roughly use the same formula.

They don't start out running mass media 'brand awareness' ads. They start out **hammering home a USP** and using mostly direct response ads.

Coca-Cola started out using coupons, forcing distribution, and selling a whole lot of sugar water as a result.

Turns out that big dumb companies start out as small smart companies. Then they hit critical mass, the board of directors takes over, HR comes on, middle management entrenches itself, there's unlimited budget — and the stupidness begins.

If you're not at that level yet, you probably want to make sure your ads have some ROI. That means being specific, targeted, and direct — not spraying your logo everywhere and hoping for the best.

Talk soon,

**The AKW Marketing Team**

posts.title: Do Less
posts.excerpt: You need to start doing less. You'll get way more done. Allow us to explain.
posts.content:
Hi,

You need to start doing less.

You'll get way more done. By doing less.

Allow us to explain.

Running a business is overwhelming. You're responsible for everything, so you need to oversee EVERYTHING.

And everything? That's a lot!

Gets frustrating. Stressful. Annoying.

Now, let's be real with each other: some stress is fine. It means things are moving.

But here's the truth: you're most productive when you're right at the edge of being in control. You know the feeling — things are moving fast, a lot is going on... but you can still keep up.

Go over the edge and things start getting out of control quickly.

As soon as you find yourself in that position, you need to look at your to-do list and figure out what you can **STOP** doing.

Maybe you need to focus on one platform only and crush it there instead of halfheartedly doing every single social media platform?

Maybe you need to zoom in on the weakest part of your funnel instead of trying to fix everything at once?

Maybe you need to focus on selling just your most profitable products or services instead of trying to be everything to everyone?

It's different for everyone. But every client we've worked with had things on their list they needed to STOP doing.

So start doing less. It will allow you to do a few things very, very well.

Feels weird. But it works.

Talk soon,

**The AKW Marketing Team**

posts.title: Why Bother?
posts.excerpt: Seeing your company in the top 3 in Google sounds nice and everything, but… is it even worth the trouble and the hassle and the work?
posts.content:
Hi,

Seeing your company in the top 3 in Google sounds nice and everything, but...

... is it even worth the trouble and the hassle and the work?

You have a thousand things on your list already. And if you're like me I assume you're not looking for ANOTHER thing to add.

And yes — I know that I'm supposed to say that the answer is **'of course this is important, drop everything you're doing and make it the #1 priority'**.

Because we do this all day, every day. And we sell the service. So we're about as fair and unbiased as a medieval witch hunter that just rode into a village with a suspiciously bad harvest.

Let me just give you three things that we know to be true and that are pretty easy to verify:

1. The top 3 businesses showing up for a Google search get basically **ALL the traffic**. The percentage is something like 78% of visitors click on the top 3. So everyone below that? They're fighting for scraps.

2. That also means that the top 3 gets basically all the calls, all the clicks, all the clients, all the attention, all the reputation boost etc. etc. etc. You get the idea.

Which leads us to the main million dollar question:

3. If you got in the top 3 and you started getting the calls and clicks that your competition is getting now...

...would you be able to land more clients?

**If the answer is YES** → getting to the top 3 is almost certainly worth it.

**If the answer is NO** → don't bother with this. It's probably not worth your time.

For now the question kinda comes down to: *'are you open to getting more clients?'*

Because if you are, this should be near the top of your marketing to-do list.

Talk soon,

**The AKW Marketing Team**

posts.title: Using Retargeting to Get More Clients and Close More Sales
posts.excerpt: Ever had the experience where some product just keeps chasing you online? It's called retargeting — and it's a shame it's used so sloppily. Here's how to do it right.
posts.content:
Hi,

Ever had the experience where some product just keeps chasing you?

You check out a lawnmower or powerdrill and before you know it your internet feed gets haunted for a full week, showing you the same ads everywhere you go.

It's called **retargeting** — and it's a shame that it's used in such a sloppy way. Because not only is there a way to make this work, if you use it right it will give you some of the best return on investment on your marketing dollars.

Let me show you how to use this in a way that is not stalkerish or annoying.

## Why You Should Care About the Customer Journey

Unless you sell something like a chocolate bar, your clients don't just randomly buy from you. There's always a lead-up time — a period where your prospects weigh their options.

Here's the rough process for almost every product or service:

1. Prospect becomes aware of a problem or need.
2. Prospect decides to do something about it.
3. Prospect looks up possible options and solutions.
4. Prospect picks an option and checks out different suppliers.
5. Prospect buys from a supplier.

Here's why this matters: **the sooner you can get in front of a prospect, the higher the chances of converting them — and the less it costs you to make a sale.**

If you find them at stage 5, they're just price shopping. You're entering the race late.

Ideally you want to get to them in stage 3. They start looking for solutions and BOOM, there you are.

## Solving the Attention Span Problem

The average attention span of a prospect is horrendous. The chances of them remembering you after they click away are dreadful.

So let's fix that.

Instead of showing people the same picture and the same ad over and over, we're going to do something different.

We're going to show them **new information and content they haven't seen before**. Maybe we record three, four, five videos, each highlighting something crucial that your future client needs to know. Useful info that actually helps them.

Then we retarget people that saw our ads before, showing them new information — helping them out long before money changes hands.

## Exploiting the Reciprocity Reflex (in a Good Way)

If someone helps you out without asking for anything in return... something kicks in. A sense of: *'this person did something for us. If we get a chance to help we should return the favor.'*

Reciprocity is built in to our psyche. And we can use it — in a good way — when we do our marketing.

The trick is to help people by **actually helping them**.

Get this right and you won't have to hard-close anyone. By the time they talk to you they already think highly of you.

Talk soon,

**The AKW Marketing Team**

posts.title: Do You Make This Mistake in Marketing?
posts.excerpt: One is the worst number in business. One key staff person. One source of leads. One big client. Here's why and what to do instead.
posts.content:
Hi,

Once upon a time, an ad account for a real estate business was doing very well. Spending over $1,000/day using Google AdWords with a ROAS of around 5.

Meaning: for every $1 put in, $5 came back.

That's so good it should be illegal.

And then — like Icarus flying too close to the sun — came the fall.

## The Worst Business Mistake

One day, login in and the Google account is blocked. Assumed it was a hiccup. Went to lunch. Didn't stress.

A few hours go by. Still blocked. Customer service is impossible to reach. Even if you spend $30,000/month you're still a small fish.

Three days go by. Finally an answer: the ad account was blocked because someone somewhere thought the ads were 'possibly misleading'.

Regular real estate ads. Nothing particularly weird.

And in the meantime? ZERO leads coming in.

Why?

Because of dependence on **ONE source of leads**. And that's the dumbest possible thing you can ever do.

## The Worst Number in Business

It's tempting to blame Google and Big Tech.

But the truth is: **this was entirely avoidable**.

One is the worst number in business.

- One key staff person.
- One source of leads.
- One big client.

And what happens when your ONE is taken away? You're dead in the water.

## Making Your Marketing Hard to Kill

Spot the "ones" in your business. Every 'one' is a vulnerability waiting to be exploited.

When it comes to marketing this means: always look to get an ad to work... and then branch it out across many different platforms.

Meta ads working? Awesome. Let's look at:
- YouTube
- Google
- Offline
- Direct mail
- Cold email
- Referral marketing
- And anything else we can think of

This is the only dependable way to become 'Hard to Kill'.

Talk soon,

**The AKW Marketing Team**

posts.title: Achieving Top of Mind Awareness in Your Market
posts.excerpt: Think about cola — what brand comes to mind? Ideally, every potential customer in your area thinks of YOU first. Here's how to make that happen.
posts.content:
Hi,

Plenty of brands and companies have top of mind awareness.

Think about cola — what brand comes to mind? Think about a search engine — what brand comes to mind?

You've answered these in your mind. Which is the entire premise of Top of Mind Awareness. Think of a subject and something is at the top of the pile.

Ideally, every potential customer in your area thinks of **you** when they think of the product or service you sell and the problem you solve.

So let's talk about how to make that happen.

## Introducing a CTA to Crush the Competition

CTA stands for Call To Action. And it's the best way — by far — to build that coveted top of mind awareness.

## How to Set Up a Funnel to Catch Clients

Let's say you run a service business. Could be accounting, could be real estate, could be a law firm or any other service.

How would you get the word out?

Maybe you'd run ads. Maybe you'd put up a sign. Maybe you'd tell friends and family.

Maybe you'd do all of the above. That'd be a great start.

Now add a CTA to that and everything gets supercharged.

Something like:
- *'Download your free guide to do X'*
- *'Put your email here and we'll send you the best way to do Y'*
- *'Text us today and we'll tell you exactly how to do Z'*

Something that gives them a reason to respond. A reason to raise their hand and say: "Yes, please get in touch with me."

## How to Instantly Upgrade Your Advertising

Adding a CTA makes everything better. It allows you to attract both customers that are ready to buy NOW and customers that are still thinking about it.

You build a list — a group of people interested in what you're selling. You're building marketing equity for both today AND tomorrow.

So let's start adding CTAs to your marketing. It's easy, doesn't cost anything, and it can change EVERYTHING for you.

Talk soon,

**The AKW Marketing Team**

posts.title: How to Write Ads, Reports, Blog Posts, and Scripts That Sell
posts.excerpt: The Pareto Principle says 20% of content gets 80% of the views. Dead wrong. It's more like 5% gets 95%. Here's how to be in that 5%.
posts.content:
Hi,

The Pareto Principle states that 20% of content online gets 80% of the views.

It's dead wrong.

It's more like 5% of content gets 95% of views.

You know why?

Because most content is BOOOOOOOOOOORING.

Repetitive. Cliché. Dry as your tongue when you wake up with an epic hangover.

So here's what you do to get your content into that epic 5%.

## Stop Writing Like a Wet Noodle

Inject some dynamite into your copy.

Best way to do it? **Write like you're having a conversation with a good friend.** Keep it casual, keep it real.

That means a lot of short, punchy sentences. Every once in a while a sentence can go on for longer, but most will be pithy and quick and to the point.

Break up those endless Tolkien-sized paragraphs. Ain't nobody got time for that!

We need to make it EASY to read, easy to skim through.

## Using Razor-Sharp Hooks That Grab Your Reader

You've got to hook your reader AND keep them there.

Make it impossible to put your stuff down. Get them to read that first sentence and then the next... and the next...

So let's not do any of this:

*"We're really good at what we do and the competition is bad and we've been in business for 20 years and we really care about you as a customer."*

That stuff is weaker than a vegan bodybuilder. It's what your competitors are saying. It's predictable. Worst of all?

It's boring. And boring doesn't pay the bills.

## Make It All About THEM

Nobody gives a rat's behind about us. Everyone cares about themselves.

Only when they believe and understand that you're actually trying to help them are they ready to hear your story.

So keep it laser-focused on how reading your stuff will help THEM.

## Skip the Fluff

Don't dance around their skepticism and objections.

Address possible objections and issues head on. Call out what they're probably thinking and then defuse it with logic, empathy, and cold hard facts. Just be real with people.

Remember this quote by the OG of advertising:

> *"The consumer is not a moron. She's your wife."* — David Ogilvy

Now let's get to WORK!

Talk soon,

**The AKW Marketing Team**

posts.title: Three Letters That Will Magically Get You More Clients
posts.excerpt: The #1 thing you can do to make your marketing pay off is craft an RSO — a Rock Solid Offer. Here's what that means and how to do it.
posts.content:
Hi,

The number one thing you can do to make marketing for your business pay off is: craft an RSO.

A **Rock Solid Offer**.

Here's how:

## The Deadliest Mistake When Crafting an Offer

Let's say we run a marketing agency and we need to come up with a good offer to attract clients.

Most business owners will come up with something like:

- *'Call us today for excellent customer service and competitive pricing'*
- *'We've been in business for 15 years and we're experts in our field'*
- *'We can handle your ads and we've done this for 100+ other customers'*

Look around you and you'll see this type of marketing EVERYWHERE.

Here's the major problem with it:

It's B-O-R-I-N-G.

Generic. Doesn't stand out. Doesn't get your prospect's blood running. The competition can say the exact same thing.

## The First Element of Your RSO

You don't fix 'the boring problem' by being outrageous — laser shows, blinking lights, airhorn noises.

That's not what it means.

Oil changes are very boring to most people. But if your car is telling you it's almost time for an oil change? All of a sudden it shoots to the top of your interest list.

You start looking for oil changes. And what do you see?

- *'Changing your oil is important and good for the engine'*
- *'$150 oil change. Book here'*

All of that doesn't cut it. Because it doesn't step into YOUR world — the world of your customer.

If your main question is *"How long is this going to take?"* then the offer that cuts through is:

**'Book your 15-minute oil change online. Fixed in no time flat.'**

That's a great start. You fix 'the boring problem' by thinking about your customer, stepping into their world, entering the conversation going on in their mind.

That's only one element of a great RSO. A solid RSO usually has three — so we still have two more to go. We'll talk about those in the next article.

Talk soon,

**The AKW Marketing Team**

posts.title: Why Spray-and-Pray Marketing Is a Surefire Way to Waste Your Ad Budget
posts.excerpt: Spending money on ads without knowing if they'll bring in a single customer is scary. Let's fix that — starting with the #1 reason ads fail.
posts.content:
Hi,

Spending money on ads is scary because you just don't know if that money is coming back. Hopefully bringing some of its friends.

So let's fix that and start with the first and biggest reason for why ads fail:

## Stop Blasting Your Message Out to Anyone With a Pulse

Before anyone's gonna shell out their hard-earned money for what you're selling, you need to make them sit up and pay attention. And the cold, hard truth is, most businesses are boring.

But here's the thing: even if you're selling the most boring thing in the world, the RIGHT customer is going to be all over it.

The key is figuring out who those people are and speaking directly to them.

## Forget the Masses — Zero In on Your Dream Buyer

Instead of playing the numbers game and hoping you'll stumble across a few decent prospects, you need to get surgical. Meticulous. Precise.

Dig deep and figure out EXACTLY who your perfect customer is.

What keeps them up at night? What problems are they trying to solve? Once you know what makes them tick, you can craft an offer that'll have them whipping out their wallets.

## Turn Dull Products Into Must-Have Solutions

I know what you're thinking: *"But my product isn't exactly exciting! How do I spruce that up?"*

You've got to find the angle that'll make your ideal customer's ears perk up. Highlight the hidden benefits, tap into their emotions, make them feel like their life won't be complete without your solution.

When you're laser-focused on your dream buyer, you don't need to carpet-bomb the entire internet with your ads. You can get your message in front of the EXACT right people, without blowing your whole budget on tire-kickers.

So quit the spray-and-pray marketing and start getting intimate with the customers who are practically BEGGING to work with you.

Talk soon,

**The AKW Marketing Team**

posts.title: Mass Marketing Doesn't Work — Do This Instead
posts.excerpt: Quick question: who's your ideal customer? A lot of business owners answer 'anyone with a pulse and money.' Two problems with that.
posts.content:
Hi,

Quick question: who's your ideal customer?

A lot of business owners answer that question with a variation of:

*'Anyone with a pulse and the money to pay me.'*

Two problems with that:

1. It doesn't narrow things down a lot.
2. It only works if you have an unlimited marketing budget.

If we're trying to reach everyone that fits that description, a couple hundred million dollars are a nice start for the marketing campaign.

But what if you're working with a marketing budget that's a bit more modest than that? Well, this article is for you.

## Why Carpet Bomb Marketing Doesn't Work

We all grew up looking at mass marketing. Coca-Cola, McDonald's, Apple. These companies are so omnipresent that it's almost hard to imagine a world without them.

Then we start our company. And we realize we lack the means to market like they do. We simply don't have the budget to saturate the market with our message.

Carpet bombing your slogan or your logo doesn't work unless you're a billion-dollar business. And it's not even how those big brands started out.

Every big brand you know started by using the same mechanism.

They crafted an **RSO** — a **Rock Solid Offer**. An offer that directly spoke to their ideal clients.

## Dynamite Marketing With Your RSO

There's a thing called 'blast fishing' where fishermen figured out that fishing was a whole lot easier if you just chucked a stick of dynamite into the water. Fish get dazed by the blast, you just scoop them up.

That's what an RSO will do for you in your market. Not only will your ideal clients be magnetically attracted to your message — if your offer is solid you'll also attract the people that are thinking about it, considering it. You'll scoop up ALL the fish.

So how do you put together an RSO? We'll talk about that in the next post.

Talk soon,

**The AKW Marketing Team**

posts.title: Why You Should Always Be Thinking About New Ads
posts.excerpt: "Hey, what's new?" — Not "what's old?" 'NEW' is exciting. And that's exactly why business owners can never rest on their laurels.
posts.content:
Hi,

"Heyyyyyy, what's new with you!?"

Pretty common way to greet someone when you haven't seen them for a while.

Notice that we don't ask:

"Hey, what's old?"

or

"Hey, tell me what I already know."

We ask what's **NEW**. Because 'NEW' is exciting! And that's exactly why as business owners we can never rest on our laurels.

## Why Ad Fatigue Is the REAL Problem

Social media is awesome in a lot of ways. Easy access to our target market, great potential to go viral, and it's never been easier to get in front of the perfect prospect for our business.

But... there are downsides.

First and foremost — attention span. We all know the TikTok brain phenomenon happening in real time. All of our clients have a reduced attention span. Not because they want to. Because they NEED to.

How else are you going to deal with ads machine-gunning at you 24/7/365? It's impossible!

## How to Keep Your Prospect Intrigued

The solution to shortened attention span is not to turn all your content into easily digestible 60-second chunks.

The solution is to offer your prospect a LOT of different content.

Don't give them 1 video. Give them 10.

Don't give them 1 article. Give them 100.

Don't give them 1 tweet. Give them 1000.

If a prospect is really interested in your stuff they'll do their own research. But there has to be depth to it.

So if you're running 1 ad now? It's time to do at least 3 different ones.

If you have 1 video in your retargeting campaign? It's time to do 5–10 others.

Go out there and be fruitful. With your content, obviously.

Talk soon,

**The AKW Marketing Team**

posts.title: Quick Way to Get Higher in Google
posts.excerpt: Got a super easy way to rank higher in Google for you. Zero technical knowledge needed — and you can implement it today.
posts.content:
Hi,

Got a super easy way to rank higher in Google for you. Zero technical knowledge needed.

If you run a business you get reviews. Hopefully they're good. Hopefully you get them somewhat regularly.

Most businesses get reviews and they do one of two things:

1. They are happy with the review but don't respond to it.
2. They respond with a polite but generic response like: *"Thank you so much for your kind review, we really appreciate it!"*

Number 2 is better than number 1. You should respond to reviews — it's a great idea.

But here's the thing.

Google is a big robot. It's crawling your profile all the time to figure out what you do and where you do it.

Everything you can do to help Google make sense of **what** you do and **where** you do it? That's a good thing.

So instead of just politely responding, make sure your response has keywords you're trying to rank for.

If you're a tree surgeon in London and you want to get more jobs in West London, instead of a generic thanks, you'd reply:

> *Thank you so much for the kind review. It was our pleasure to remove your trees in West London. We're doing more and more jobs in West — not just in Chelsea but also Kensington and Ealing. Would love to help you in the future with any of your forestry needs, be it tree removal, crown removal, tree trimming, pruning, and anything else!*

That gives the Google bot a full five-course meal instead of throwing it some scraps.

Really helps with SEO results. Try it out today!

Talk soon,

**The AKW Marketing Team**

posts.title: How to Rank Higher in Google Tomorrow
posts.excerpt: Got a trick for you. It works extremely fast and it is very reliable. Here's the grey-hat move that's 100% within the rules.
posts.content:
Hi,

Got a trick for you. Will be helpful.

It works extremely fast and it is very reliable.

If you feel a "but" coming in this story... you're right. Because we'll be pushing the rules a little bit with this one.

No worries — we won't go **against** the rules if you do this right. It's more of a grey-hat thing instead of a black-hat thing.

Here's the key insight: look at the top 3 results for almost any local service search on Google. They ALL have the keyword (or at least part of it) in their business name — for example, **"pest control"** or **"pest control London"**.

That weighs very heavily in your favor in Google rankings.

So what do you do if your company name doesn't have those keywords in it? Do you just add it to your GBP name anyway?

You could — and a lot of companies do. BUT that can get you in trouble with Google, which is why we wouldn't recommend it. The rule is that you should use your **real business name** in your GBP. If you add keywords to the business name and a competitor reports you, Google may do a manual check. Can't verify it? You lose the ranking boost — or worse, get kicked out entirely.

That's why we need a workaround. Introducing: **The DBA**.

DBA stands for "Doing Business As". In some other countries it's known as a 'trading name' or 'alternative business name'.

It's easy to register, very low cost, and in some countries even free.

But the best part? This is now an **official name** for your company.

So you can safely change your GBP title to your DBA name — adding the right keywords — and if Google ever asks you to verify it, you just show them the paperwork. You're not breaking the rules anymore. You're working within the rules.

Handle the DBA, change your business name in GBP by adding the right keywords, and enjoy a big ranking boost right away.

Talk soon,

**The AKW Marketing Team**

posts.title: AI Slop Is the Worst
posts.excerpt: Every year someone tells us a new AI model has 'changed the game.' Every year we try it. Every year it produces pure slop. Here's the real lesson.
posts.content:
Hi,

In the past few years we've had people tell us we could "build an AI model" off our newsletters.

*"You won't have to write anything yourself anymore! It will sound just like you!"*

Roughly every year or so we give it a try. Usually when someone tells us enough times that this NEW AI model has changed the game. This time it's real, this time it's going to be amazing, trust me bro!

So we train it on our materials. We've tried every variation. It doesn't matter how much data you cram into the model.

It always produces pure slop.

Every. Single. Time.

There are two possible explanations:

1. Our writing is just pure slop and we're deluding ourselves into thinking otherwise.
2. AI does not create anything. It just rehashes what you give it, resulting in some kind of weird word-smoothie that vaguely resembles things you said in the past.

*(We're pretty sure it's the 2nd one.)*

AI will never be more creative than a human being. If AI can out-write you, out-creative you, out-sell you... you haven't put enough skill-points in that particular skill. Because it's not hard to outperform a machine in tasks that are not suited for a machine.

We use AI all the time for tasks that are extremely suited for a machine — automating processes, data analysis, scheduling.

But human to human? That's a human task. And no computer will ever outperform you in that.

Talk soon,

**The AKW Marketing Team**

posts.title: Get More Done
posts.excerpt: I've studied every time management system under the sun over the past 20 years. They all have the same problem: the system takes too long to run. Here's the simple fix.
posts.content:
Hi,

I usually do my weekly planning on Monday. There was a time when it took me hours just to get ready for the week. Now I get it done in less than 15 minutes.

Over the past 20 years I've basically studied every time management system under the sun. And they all have the same issue.

It takes **too damn long** to run the system.

I remember trying out a system that had me do a weekly review on Sunday. Nothing wrong with that. But I followed every step, did the review exactly their way... and it took me 4.5 hours!

That's a ridiculous amount of time.

So I went to their online forums to ask if this was normal. One of their trainers got back to me and after some back and forth basically said: *'well, no one ACTUALLY follows all those steps. That would take way too long'*.

That's like having a training schedule and the trainer that made it tells you: *"Well, no one really does all these exercises."*

Makes no sense.

So here's how we handle time management.

You only need two things:

1. A calendar
2. A list

We use Google Calendar. You can use anything similar. For the list, switch between regular paper, Kanbanflow, or a plain .txt file — whatever fits your schedule.

Planning the week and the day is easy:

1. All time-sensitive stuff goes in the calendar. If you have to show up somewhere at 11? That doesn't go on your list. It goes in your calendar.
2. All your to-do items go on your to-do list.
3. Go over the items and give them an A, B, or C.

**A = HAS TO BE DONE TODAY**

**B = WOULD BE NICE TODAY**

**C = SOME TIME IN THE NEXT 7 DAYS**

Then pick an A1, an A2, and an A3. Leave the rest alone.

Then get to work on A1.

It's that easy.

And because it's that simple, people tend to IMMEDIATELY want to complicate it.

"Let me order all the A items"

"Let me add an extra category"

"Let me automate it using AI"

Our advice: just don't. Run the system as laid out above. It's easy. It works. Would highly recommend.

Talk soon,

**The AKW Marketing Team**
